summary: Prospect Hill fire tower in Waltham: 58-foot original, 68-foot steel tower built 1964, used until 1977; sold and moved to Tennessee in 2007.

facts.design: Original 58-foot tower on city land; 68-foot steel tower built in 1964, called the last one standing (FFLOS)
facts.status_note: Closed after the 1977 fire season; sold by the state and moved to Tennessee in 2007. The Tennessee site is not identified in any source read.

events.note: Wikipedia dates a fire tower on Big Prospect to 1917; FFLOS gives no date for its original 58-foot tower

resolved_conflicts.field: location of the tower after 1963 and the Tennessee structure
resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia says the fire tower moved to Little Prospect and later carried Waltham Amateur Radio Association equipment. A community photo page says a tower on the hill is now that group's repeater site. The 2007 chapter report says the closed Waltham tower went to Tennessee. The sources do not identify which structure is which, so the story reports the accounts side by side.

sources.title: Photographs of Prospect Hill Park, Waltham, MA

notes_for_editor: Tennessee destination not found: the tnlandforms.us Tennessee tower list has no Waltham or Massachusetts entry. Pennsylvania 'Prospect Hill' fire tower pages (lumberheritage.org, mchsmuseum.org) describe a different site and were not used. The Waltham Land Trust page mentions a 'long-abandoned Air Force tower' at the summit; not used as a fire-lookout source. A Facebook snippet from the FFLA Massachusetts chapter says the tower closed for 1974 and reopened 1975 to 1977; it could not be fetched, so it is not cited. Wikipedia's 1917 date may or may not be the same structure as FFLOS's undated original.
